facts.raw_span: born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation
weighing 2152 g
one of monochorionic diamniotic twins
her identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
Fetal ultrasound had shown microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
Postnatal MRI of the head revealed microcephaly, marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles without signs of elevated intracranial pressure
severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum were preserved
No intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions were seen
very weak light reflexes bilaterally
mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign
No chorioretinal dysplasia was noted

concepts.why: The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes, along with the preservation of the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum, is consistent with this diagnosis.
The presence of very weak light reflexes, mild optic nerve pallor, and suspected peripapillary double-ring sign, in the absence of chorioretinal dysplasia, suggests this diagnosis.

The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes, along with the presence of mild optic nerve pallor, is consistent with this diagnosis.

It explains the marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles without signs of elevated intracranial pressure.

rationales.F04: Twin death in utero could be related to Fetal akinesia deformation sequence
rationales.F05: Microcephaly and ventricular enlargement are characteristic of several neurodevelopmental disorders
rationales.F06: Postnatal MRI findings support the presence of severe brain abnormalities
rationales.F07: Severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes is a distinctive feature of some neurodevelopmental disorders
rationales.F10: Weak light reflexes could be related to visual impairment, as seen in Leber congenital amaurosis
rationales.F11: Optic nerve pallor and peripapillary double-ring sign could be related to Leber congenital amaurosis or other retinal dystrophies

frontier_selector.rationale: Walker-Warburg syndrome explains microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign, while Zellweger spectrum disorder also explains some of these findings but lacks specific eye abnormalities mentioned in the vignette.
